A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MotionStream and contain readable main sections and appendices A–G. Their text, equations, tables and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original motion-transfer and novel-view-synthesis experiments, ablations, VAE evaluations, VBench results and a user study in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental outcomes, including Tables 1–4, Tables A1–A4 and the user-study results in Figure A1.

M1.justification: The motion encoder, teacher/student architecture, joint guidance, distillation objectives, attention sinks and rolling cache are retained. Section 3.2 clarifies implementation of the existing Self Forcing gradient-truncation strategy without establishing a changed training procedure.

E1.justification: Training coverage remains OpenVid-1M and synthetic Wan videos; evaluation retains DAVIS, Sora, extended Sora and LLFF. Figure 8 adds an example within the existing interactive-control task, not a distinct dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Image Conductor, Go-With-The-Flow, Diffusion-As-Shader and ATI for motion transfer, and DepthSplat, ViewCrafter and SEVA for novel-view synthesis. Appendix VAE and generative-quality comparator sets also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 and Appendices B, D and E retain the same sample counts, preprocessing, resolutions, metrics, training budgets and baseline-specific evaluation settings. The added demo introduces no new reported evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Figure 8 adds a qualitative case showing generation responding to successive online user controls. Existing guidance, attention, sampling-step, VAE and dropped-motion ablations, together with the failure analyses, are unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 4 retains identical latency and throughput variability reporting. v3 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 1–4 and A1–A4 and the existing plotted results match. v3 adds Figure 8's demo outputs and corrects Table 4's qualitative attribution of stable high-quality generation from c3s0w1 to c3s1w1, consistent with the unchanged table rows.

T1.justification: The track representation, attention-context definitions, guidance equations and distillation mathematics remain unchanged, including Equations 1–4 and A1–A2. Minor notation corrections add no mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about real-time streaming motion control, long-video stability, efficient causal distillation and state-of-the-art performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of attention sinks, error accumulation, guidance tradeoffs and backbone differences are retained, as are Appendix F's limitations. The corrected Table 4 caption agrees with the attention-sink interpretation already stated in v2.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 revises the gradient-truncation documentation: v2 describes retaining graphs for final denoised KV embeddings; v3 explicitly describes detaching previous-frame KV and restricting gradients to the selected denoising step of the current block. Other training details and resource-access statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited research and substantive positioning are retained. Wan's duplicate reference entries are consolidated, TrajectoryCrafter receives publication metadata, and citation labels are corrected; these do not introduce or remove distinct prior works.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited grammar and terminology corrections, expands the gradient-truncation paragraph, adds a demo pointer and acknowledgments, and updates affiliations and the conference header. The narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is reformatted, Figure 7 moves from page 9 to page 10, and Figure 8 adds a streaming-demo sequence. Table 4's caption and Figure A1's DAS labels are corrected, alongside localized page reflow.

improvement.justification: v3 makes gradient handling more explicit and resolves the contradiction between Table 4's caption and its data, improving implementation clarity and interpretability. The new interactive example and editorial cleanup also help presentation. These are limited gains; the quantitative evidence and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
